newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian exchange plans new list, Pennu to join.
newsitem.headline: Estonian exchange plans new list, Pennu to join.

text.p: The Tallinn stock exchange said on Friday it was planning to launch a new secondary list for small to medium-sized companies and that computer firm Pennu would be the first on the list.
The list will be launched on October 3.
"The new secondary list is aimed at smaller, younger and riskier companies," Tallinn stock exchange managing director Helo Meigas told Reuters.
Pennu is Estonia's second largest computer firm and recently placed shares with international and local investors.
The exchange currently has a main list, that quotes the country's top five banks.
There is also a free market list, which includes stocks which are traded over the counter but which can be traced real-time through the exchange's automated computer system.
The new list will be for companies that have a market capitalisation of at least 10 million kroons, at least 100 investors and can publish their last two balance sheets.
Free market companies have fewer obligations, including the need to register their shares with the central depository.
Official list members need market capitalisation of at least 100 million kroons and publish their last three years results.
Pennu has around 25 to 30 percent of the computer market in Estonia and last year had sales of 65 million kroons and 3.3 million kroon profit.
"We are eager to join the main list but it will probably happen after three years when we have increased our capital," Alo Koop, Pennu chairman, told Reuters.
